clue.text: Possibly inaccurate, but right for new cartoon?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged some other way, so they are reworked
the abbreviation R (right) is put in place of N (new) in the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cartoon can be inaccurate yet still right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but right for new' swaps the N of INACCURATE for R, giving IRACCURATE, and 'Possibly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is an exaggerated satirical drawing of a person, a kind of cartoon.

clue.text: One escaping head cook

indicators.note: the one getting away means it leaves the word for head

parts.note: a head or boss is a chief
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The head cook makes a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' takes I (one) out of CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a kitchen.

clue.text: Painter showing back in bizarre portrait

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A strange portrait shows someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals letters inside 'bizarre portrait'; 'back' reads EPOR the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: On a boat, a painter is the line used to tie it up, a nautical sense of the word.

clue.text: One's pushed out and given the brush-off in sport

definitions.text: One's pushed out and given the brush-off in sport

parts.words: One's pushed out and given the brush-off in sport
parts.note: the object in a sport on ice is slid away from the player while teammates sweep the ice ahead of it with brooms

explanation.walkthrough: 'brush-off' sounds like rejection, but the sweepers really do brush the ice in front of the sliding granite object.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game played on ice, the heavy granite piece is pushed off and swept along with brushes.

clue.text: Powers support most of article

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: most of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: the definite article is the word 'the'

explanation.surface: Powers are said to back up most of an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the article's last letter. 'Powers' is the definition in the sense of a law given real force.
explanation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has real force; teeth means effective powers of enforcement.

clue.text: Particular people run in socks -I run in shoes!

parts.note: a race is a particular people or ethnic group

indicators.note: in puts the run inside the word for socks

parts.note: hose are stockings or socks
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone running in socks contrasts with a speaker running in shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside HOSE. The definition speaks as the animal, which runs wearing horseshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing thoroughbred runs fitted with metal shoes, so the speaker is a galloping animal.

clue.text: Fairy-tale writer avoiding ending that's depressing

indicators.note: avoiding its ending means the writer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the brothers Grimm wrote fairy tales

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale writer steers clear of a depressing ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding ending' cuts the last M from GRIMM.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means gloomy or bleak, synonyms for depressing.

clue.text: Greg's extremities in lather, suffering? It's 90%!

indicators.note: suffering means the letters are in a bad way and get rearranged
the extremities of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Greg is in a lather, his hands and feet suffering, and someone puts the pain at 90 percent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremities' gives G and G from Greg's; 'suffering' rearranges GG with IN and LATHER. The % is a print slip for the degree sign: 90 degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle of exactly ninety degrees is the square corner of geometry.

clue.text: Unpleasant of French to call without coming to the point

parts.note: mean means unkind or unpleasant
de is French for of
to ring is to telephone, to call

explanation.surface: Someone unpleasant calls in French without getting to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Meandering talk wanders about and never gets to its point.

clue.text: Feel passion returning when apprehended by old coppers

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: apprehended means caught, so the reversed word is held inside the others

parts.note: copper coins are pence

indicators.note: returning means the word for passion is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: Feeling passion when arrested by former police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reads the passion backwards and 'when apprehended by' holds it inside the old coins. 'coppers' suggests police but means copper coins, pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to undergo or feel it.

clue.text: Muslim commander imprisoning king in Indian city

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding the king inside the commander

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman commander or chief
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Muslim commander locks up a king in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoning' puts R inside AGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the city in Uttar Pradesh where the Taj Mahal stands.

clue.text: Behaviour that's above board?

parts.note: honest conduct, read literally as how one conducts oneself over the dinner table

explanation.walkthrough: 'above board' usually means honest; here it means literally over the table where you eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette at meals is conduct shown over the dining surface.

clue.text: Land, ploughed earth, arable ground ultimately without depth?

parts.note: to light on something is to land or settle on it

indicators.note: ploughed earth is turned over, so its letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Farmland of ploughed earth and arable ground is shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughed' rearranges EARTH into HEART; 'ultimately' takes E and D from arable and ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful and carefree, lacking seriousness or gravity.

clue.text: An act with cross, possibly of a devotional nature

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might form something else, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An act involving a cross may be religious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges AN ACT with CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanct means sacred, regarded as too holy to violate.

clue.text: Rich vocal arrangement with dead keyboard instrument

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on gravestones and in records

explanation.surface: A rich vocal arrangement accompanied by a dead keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges RICH VOCAL, then D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavichord is an early stringed keyboard with a soft tone.

clue.text: Reptile masquerading as a log with tail, right?

indicators.note: masquerading as something means disguised, so these letters appear in another form

explanation.surface: A reptile is disguised as a log with its tail showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masquerading' rearranges A LOG with TAIL, then R ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian reptile of the Americas and China.

clue.text: Source of food cooked for a mutt, right? For a mog, surely!

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Food cooked for a dog, but a cat would surely want fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges FOR A MUTT with R. 'For a mog, surely!' adds that the fishy source suits a cat; mog is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm raises fish to be eaten, so it is a supplier of food.

clue.text: Individual caught between two sides?

indicators.note: caught between means held inside the two side letters

parts.note: left and right are the two sides, L and R
an individual is one

explanation.surface: A single person is trapped between two opposing camps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught between' puts ONE between L and R; the whole clue also describes the solitary person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps apart from others is a solitary person, alone between factions.

clue.text: Fix hedge, clipping front

indicators.note: clipping its front means the hedge loses its first letter

parts.note: privet is a common hedge shrub

explanation.surface: Fix the hedge by trimming the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipping front' removes P from PRIVET.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten firmly, to fix in place.

clue.text: Zero information given to me, beginning to live on fruit

parts.note: zero is the letter O
gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone told nothing decides to begin living on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information. 'beginning to' takes L from live.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ogen is a small sweet variety of melon, a fruit.

clue.text: Almost 1300 hours when name's brought in? Excellent

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the time phrase

parts.note: a moment short of one o'clock in the afternoon is a second to one
N is short for name

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is nearly one o'clock when a name is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts N into SECOND TO ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsurpassed by anyone means the best, superb.

clue.text: Pacific territory, note, linked to gold and rugby

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RU is short for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A Pacific island is described with notes on its gold and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small island republic in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Greek character going to doctor, having lost feeling

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A Greek character visits a doctor after losing sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means without sensation, deadened.

clue.text: Very attractive and certainly accepting kiss when getting up

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards
accepting means taking the kiss inside

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Very attractive and sure to accept a kiss on rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts X inside YES (YXES), then 'getting up' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy means sexually appealing, alluring.

clue.text: No cricket side appearing in hottest part of day?

parts.note: on is the leg side of the cricket field

explanation.surface: No cricket team turns up in the midday heat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on (leg) side is one half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is when the sun is highest, typically the warmest time.

clue.text: Non-medicinal treatment's slapdash care? Untrue

indicators.note: slapdash means careless and messy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that a drug-free remedy is careless, then denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slapdash' rearranges CARE with UNTRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy relying on diet, fresh air and herbs rather than drugs.

clue.text: Activity also involving daughter

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round the daughter letter

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: An activity that also involves one's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts D inside TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or commotion, busy activity.

clue.text: Something unexpected in store for you?

definitions.text: Something unexpected in store for you?

parts.words: Something unexpected in store for you?
parts.note: a surprise awaiting you, read literally as an unplanned purchase in a shop

explanation.walkthrough: 'in store for you' usually means coming your way; here it means bought in a shop on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur-of-the-moment purchase is unplanned shopping.
